spec.title: PROP-076 — Environment roles and explicit target binding

scope.title: 1. One package system, separate environment roles
scope.p: Code-bearing package source identity remains the shippable tree under [PROP-024](PROP-024-code-bearing-packages.xml#SHIPPABLE-TREE-DEF). Existing package build and binary delivery remain governed by [PROP-025](../modules/vibe-workspace/PROP-025-binary-delivery.xml#BINARY-MECHANISM-LOWERING). An environment does not replace Cargo/npm resolution of their internals.

p.ENVIRONMENT-ROLE-SEPARATION-LAW: An environment is a deployable consumer context for the existing package identities, requires, choices and features. It may be authored in a coding project, image repository or user directory without Git. It adds no package kind, change type or personal stewardship database. Definition, exact lock, operation executor, admitted target binding and realized generation are five different identity roles. Sharing content or equal field spellings does not collapse their authority.

p.ENVIRONMENT-DEFINITION-LAW: EnvironmentDefinition owns portable desired composition: existing package/root selections, feature/choice selections, target compatibility constraints, named tool/service exports and named runtime bindings. Its identity is supplied by its authored definition owner. Named roots here are desired resources, not machine absolute paths. Credentials, discovered HOME/PATH and physical destination identities are excluded. Construction does not resolve, install or activate packages.

p.ENVIRONMENT-LOCK-LAW: EnvironmentLock binds one definition to its exact selected Vibe captures/configuration, external backend closure references, explicit build/runtime dependency roles and target OS/architecture/ABI/libc constraints. Its identity and exact closure evidence belong to the resolving/lock owner. A package version, source URL or physical root cannot substitute for this selected closure. It is derived once for its environment domain, not a machine-global or stewardship lock.

p.EXECUTION-CONTEXT-LAW: ExecutionContext names the executor facts supplied for a particular operation: its OS/architecture/ABI, admitted tool/provider identity, principal and explicit network/mount/process capabilities. The admitting surface owns those facts and capabilities; a pure value describes them but does not grant an effect or prove admission. A local Windows process and a Linux build worker are distinct executors even when they participate in one environment operation.

p.TARGET-BINDING-LAW: TargetBinding owns the stable environment instance reference, selected generation reference when established, target OS/architecture/ABI/libc, target mode, admitted filesystem roots/prefix, target principal/home and storage-backend reference. Workspace projection, user profile, offline Linux rootfs/image and future live Linux system are target modes, not package kinds. Physical root/capability evidence belongs to the admitting storage owner and is separate from portable definition content. A pathname, same username or a copied receipt is not physical authority.

p.TARGET-INSTANCE-CONTINUITY-LAW: Cloning a definition or instantiating image content requires a new admitted instance binding; immutable generation content may be reused. Reused pathname spellings do not transfer old instance receipts. Move, relocate and adopt need their own explicit validated operations. Constructors neither discover aliases nor claim that two roots are physically disjoint.

p.ENVIRONMENT-GENERATION-LAW: EnvironmentGeneration binds its producing lock/recipes to realized payload inventory and metadata, dependency closure, generated boot/adapters/service catalog and activation references. Its identity and evidence belong to the producing generation owner. It does not itself authorize activation. Mutable application data, secrets and per-user stewardship state are outside immutable generation content. A desired definition or lock is not a realization receipt.

abi.title: 7. Executor, produced-tool runtime and emitted-code target

p.ABI-ROLE-SEPARATION-LAW: Keep three machine roles distinct: the machine executing a build, the machine on which the produced tool will run, and, when that tool is a compiler, its emitted-code target. None is inferred from another role. Native Vibe extension/library ABI belongs to the executor that loads it; an installable Linux payload belongs to its produced-tool runtime target. Compiler output constraints are separately selected and are absent when that role is not applicable.

p.COMPATIBILITY-FACTS-LAW: Compatibility decisions consume explicit role-labelled facts and admitted capabilities. OS-only equality or a when.os match does not establish architecture, libc or ABI compatibility, prefix relocatability or operation support. Missing required facts produce an explicit unresolved/refused compatibility result; an unsupported operation names its target mode or unsatisfied constraint before effectful dispatch. Describing Windows executor plus Linux target is legal data and cannot select a Windows launcher for that Linux payload.

p.LEGACY-HOST-INTERPRETATION-LAW: Existing TargetWhen and TargetApplicability retain their strict OS-set grammar and explicit legacy executor-host interpretation. Package and deploy projections continue receiving the same injected current command-process OS, with absence unconditional, existing active/skipped decisions and inactive-dependency refusals unchanged. A new target value does not silently retarget old guards. Later target-aware predicates and world/boot consumers require explicit adoption and separately bound evidence.

p.LOCAL-WORKSPACE-COMPATIBILITY-LAW: The first pure compatibility result supports an explicitly injected existing local workspace binding with legacy local semantics. The surface may explicitly bind its local destination to the observed local executor; this is a named mapping, not an inference usable for remote/image targets. Bare install still materializes package source; constructing these values never starts a build, native load, provider, deployment or activation.

p.UNSUPPORTED-TARGET-OPERATIONS-LAW: User-profile, offline rootfs/image and live-system targets are describable domain data but the initial role foundation returns explicit unsupported-operation results for their execution. Existing user-scoped deploy fields are not evidence of full environment-operation support. User HOME/rootfs/OCI delivery is a later commissioned implementation; a live distribution remains a design direction. No provider is assumed to implement every target mode.

construction.title: 9. Pure construction and existing identity owners

p.INJECTED-CONSTRUCTION-AUTHORITY-LAW: Pure constructors validate role-specific inputs, required nonblank references and cross-reference consistency without HOME/PATH lookup, filesystem probing, Docker, registry/configuration reads or execution. Root/principal/provider selection arrives from the trusted admitting surface and is not reselected below it. The existing project vibevm layout stays in place; root/prefix layout policy is separately centralized rather than invented per provider.

p.IDENTITY-OWNER-REUSE-LAW: This role foundation introduces no identity hash recipe, machine serializer/parser or wire epoch. Reuse existing package/content/capture references through their current owners; ContentHash stays a package-content reference, not an environment hasher. Where an environment-specific content-ID producer is not yet implemented, explicitly injected opaque role references support binding/equality only, never a claim of independently authenticated content. A future producer or durable format requires its own existing-owner justification and source contract before emission. Preserve role distinctions even when underlying reference strings happen to be equal.

p.PURE-ROLE-FOUNDATION-OBSERVED: The pure role foundation is implemented in `vibe-core::environment`, code subject `40ef38d10b969082bab028c6b49621af11289946`. Five producer-labelled role references and checked composition/closure joins remain supplied claims, not authenticated content or physical authority. The local compatibility result covers source projection only: unknown ABI/libc is allowed when unrequired, while explicit missing/mismatching requirements refuse. Target launcher-family descriptions and executor-native facts remain separate; user/rootfs/live operations are unsupported. Eight selected GNU/Linux cases passed; the independent export-namespace correction repeated only its one exact case. Tool and service names are checked within their separate collections. No ambient HOME/PATH, filesystem probing, Docker, provider execution, new hash/wire format or existing consumer adoption was added. This does not prove native deployment or the later layout/payload/service programme.

p.ENVIRONMENT-PROOF-BOUNDARY-LAW: The pre-foundation baseline has pure OS applicability values, Cargo binary-to-artifact lowering, current-process native platform selection and injected deployment roots. That is not evidence that these five environment objects, target ABI checks, cross-target launcher selection or HOME/rootfs/live operations are implemented. Later executable constructors and compatibility tests must cite these anchors; consumer migration and native execution proofs remain separate claims.

environment-layout-policy.title: 11. Injected environment layout and target resource policy

p.ENVIRONMENT-LAYOUT-LAW: EnvironmentLayout names configuration, immutable store, profile, mutable state and disposable cache bindings. Each is supplied, explicitly derived, inapplicable or missing-required; absence never discovers HOME/PATH. Supplied target home remains independent of settings. Constructors create nothing.

p.ENVIRONMENT-LAYOUT-DEFAULTS-LAW: Only explicit selection of the settings-anchored defaults table derives from injected target settings binding S: configuration S; immutable store S/store; mutable state S/state. These three bindings are required by this selected table; missing S leaves them missing-required/unresolved and cannot mark them inapplicable. Other explicit layout selections must state their required versus inapplicable root roles; a missing required binding never becomes inapplicable. Profile has no observed legacy directory default: workspace profile is inapplicable, otherwise require explicit binding. Disposable cache requires explicit binding when requested, otherwise is inapplicable; independent registry/search caches retain S/registries and S/search-cache. Config files remain S/config.toml, S/settings.toml and S/registry.toml; explicit config-file override stays separate. Store reuses the existing binary-CAS spelling; state is a proposed environment anchor, not migration of deployments. No raw instance/producer/reference becomes a directory component, hash or encoding. Partition names are separately target-policy checked.

p.ENVIRONMENT-RESOURCE-IDENTITY-LAW: ResourceIdentity includes environment instance, root-role/binding reference, principal, explicit target path/case policy and validated component sequence. Equal pathname text never transfers receipts between bindings. A1 physical_evidence references remain unverified supplied data; physical aliases, containment and effect admission belong to the storage owner.

p.TARGET-PATH-POLICY-LAW: Linux components reject empty, dot, dotdot, NUL and embedded slash; colon, backslash, device-like names and other valid literal bytes remain legal under Windows control. A separate macOS POSIX-byte lexical policy accepts the same component grammar but retains its own target identity; it does not guess APFS/HFS case or Unicode normalization behavior, physical aliases or content CAS. Those properties require a storage-owner observation and may be unavailable; lexical generation can still operate with an explicitly selected supported comparison rule. Windows portable-Win32 policy alone adds drive/UNC structure, reserved characters/names including COM/LPT superscript digits, trailing-dot/space restrictions. Case/collision comparison is explicitly selected lexical policy, not OS-inferred native behavior; unknown comparison is unresolved/unsupported. Generic Unicode lowercase is not an NTFS guarantee. Never apply source-portable RelPath to Linux or macOS payloads.

p.PAYLOAD-PREFIX-COMPATIBILITY-LAW: Describe relocatable payloads with producer evidence references and conditions, prefix-bound payloads with exact target-prefix constraints, or unsupported payloads with reason. Declarative matching does not verify evidence or authorize effects. Unknown relocatability cannot become relocatable because destination is HOME; changed prefix refuses prefix-bound payloads. No binary rewriting occurs.

p.RESERVED-ENVIRONMENT-RESOURCES-LAW: Account, service, mount and boot roles remain describable with explicit unsupported-operation status. Missing required bindings are unresolved; unneeded roots are inapplicable. No account provisioning, service activation, mount, privilege broker or live-system operation is implemented by layout metadata.

p.ENVIRONMENT-LAYOUT-COMPATIBILITY-BOUNDAR: Project vibevm roots and root vibe.toml remain under PROP-052. Existing vibe-bin store/bin and deployment state/deployments consumers retain their paths. New layout descriptions neither move them nor establish target operations. Consumer adoption requires separately bound amendments and proof.

environment-realization-formats.title: 12. Exact lock and realized payload contracts

p.ENVIRONMENT-FORMAT-EPOCHS-LAW: Environment definition, exact selected lock, realization request, payload inventory and generation receipt use registered epoch-one machine formats with generated readers and explicit semantic validators. Request, output, error and durable receipt carriers name their own owners and epochs; a Rust struct, private pointer or package version is not a serialized contract. Unknown members, unsupported epochs, missing required closure evidence and wrong target-role metadata refuse before an identity is published. This producer layer follows the pure opaque-reference foundation above; it does not retroactively turn its injected A.1 references into authenticated hashes or increment a package version.

p.ENVIRONMENT-EXACT-LOCK-IDENTITY-LAW: The lock owner hashes the normalized typed definition, exact selected Vibe captures and configuration, target OS/architecture/ABI/libc constraints, and complete declared build/runtime dependency roles. An external Cargo/npm or native-backend closure is carried by exact owner-produced capture/lock identities; VibeVM does not infer its internals from a URL, mutable version, provider name or ambient cache. Canonical ordering is by the validated UTF-8 role and identity bytes, with duplicate semantic keys refused. The epoch-one lock digest is SHA-256 over domain `vibevm/environment-lock/e1` followed by ordered tagged frames: each frame encodes a two-byte big-endian tag length, tag bytes, eight-byte big-endian value length and value bytes. Text values use exact validated UTF-8 bytes, integer values use unsigned eight-byte big-endian representation, booleans use one byte 0 or 1, and binary values use raw bytes. Collections encode an unsigned eight-byte big-endian count before their ordered framed elements; an optional value has a separate one-byte presence frame (0 absent, 1 present) before its value frame, so empty and absent differ. Nested structs use their registered field order, not source declaration order. The schema and producer must retain this recipe identity; reordered input declarations with equal normalized meaning give the same digest, while changed selected bytes or target constraints change it. Unknown required inputs yield unavailable proof, never a guessed exact lock.

p.ENVIRONMENT-PAYLOAD-INVENTORY-LAW: A realized generation inventories every included regular file, directory, link and supported special node under target-policy-validated relative components, with kind, exact content or link-target bytes, mode/permission, ownership/principal interpretation and the producing dependency role. Every selected file byte participates through an exact captured digest; a manifest path alone is not byte proof. Linux UID/GID are Linux-target metadata, never serialized from Windows executor IDs; Windows identity and ACL semantics require their own declared support or a typed unavailable/unsupported result. Unsupported privileged nodes, unknown metadata, alias/collision risk and unverified link targets cannot be silently dropped or reported as a complete generation.

p.ENVIRONMENT-GENERATION-IDENTITY-LAW: The realized generation receipt binds its producing exact lock, recipe/schema epochs, target role, ordered payload inventory, dependency closure and generated boot/adapter/service outputs. It computes a separate SHA-256 identity with domain `vibevm/environment-generation/e1` and the same unambiguous tagged-frame encoding; it never reuses the lock digest as proof of produced bytes. Changed payload bytes, metadata, target ABI, generated output or incomplete recursive closure change/refuse the output identity. Stable content may be shared across instances, but activation and physical target authority remain separately admitted; no receipt silently authorizes an install or substitutes for a domain journal.
